newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent levels hold soft, wet markets quiet.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent levels hold soft, wet markets quiet.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil barrels started the week on a steady but weak note and many traders expected crude to remain low for the remainder of the week.
An April 13-15 minimum sized cargo of Brent was sold by Statsco to a Wall Street refiner at May Brent -94 cents.
"The agenda is to keep Brent down this week and we should see dated (Brent) levels coming up next week," one trader said referring to the large CFD positions held by some major players.
Action was light on other North Sea crudes with most refiners seen covered through the second decade of April following active buying at the end of last week.
As outright levels regained some of Friday's losses CFDs ticked around levels seen late on Friday and trade was muted.

May Brent traded at 1705 GMT up 35 cents at $18.03 a barrel. Next weeks CFDs (Apr 14-18) were discussed at June -77/-73 cents after earlier trading at June -75 and June -73 cents. The roll into April 21-25 week was done at -10 cents.
There were no Brent cargoes in the paper chains on Monday.
There was only one Brent intermonth spread deal reported -- a May/June at -23 cents.
"It's one of the quietest days I can remember," a refinery trader said before the physical Brent cargo traded.
"Noody wants to do anything until they have a feel for where dated Brent is going to be," he said.

In the Mediterranean, traders said a narrow spread between low and high sulphur fuel oil was supporting the sour market and sellers of Urals were holding back cargoes confident of a stronger market in a few days.
"There's nothing on offer at the moment, but I think we'll see the next deal at around (Dated Brent) minus $1.25 to $1.20," a local refiner said.
Other sour grades wee also scarce, with the market for Iraqi Kirkuk dormant ahead of the 30 cents price cut in May.
A lone Syrian Light cargo loading April 22-24 was on offer at a premium of a few cents to the Official Selling Price.
Sweet West African grades were also seen on offer in the Med, but were finding virtually no buying interest, dealers said.
Traders said that Dated Brent's weakness relative to U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) meant that most marketing efforts for West African grades were focused transatlantic.
"A lot of VLCCs have been fixed for the States. It's all looking in that direction," said one trader.
"The differentials that are being talked would be ten or fifteen cents overvalued in Europe," he added.
A Qua Iboe cargo was seen offered into the U.S. Gulf Coast on Friday at Dated Brent plus $1.75 a barrel.
FOB differentials were seen steady to slightly weaker at Dated Brent plus 20 cents for gasoline-rich Bonny Light and Dated minus 20 cents for Forcados.
